summary: GridFS file-storage migration verified end-to-end. 8/8 backend tests pass against the preview URL. New uploads (library materials + student submissions) are persisted to MongoDB GridFS, downloads stream the exact bytes back, instructor AI review reads from GridFS successfully, deleting a submission cleans up its GridFS entry (no orphans), and legacy disk-only records correctly return HTTP 410 with the fix message.
passed_tests: POST /api/library/materials stores file in GridFS (gridfs_id set, file_path empty, fs.files entry matches uploaded length)
GET /api/materials/{id}/download streams GridFS bytes == upload bytes
POST /api/materials/{id}/submit (student) writes submission to GridFS (gridfs_id set, file_path empty, fs.files entry length matches)
GET /api/submissions/{id}/download (instructor/admin) returns exact uploaded bytes from GridFS
GET /api/submissions/{id} regression: returns submission with material + student info
POST /api/submissions/{id}/review reads file from GridFS and returns 200 with AI feedback (no 404/410)
DELETE /api/submissions/{id} removes submission and its GridFS file (no orphan in fs.files)
Legacy submission (file_path only, gridfs_id=null, missing disk file) -> GET /download returns HTTP 410 with clear 'no longer available' message
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:106-128 save_bytes_to_gridfs + read_bytes_from_doc correctly fall back to legacy file_path and raise a clean 410 when the disk file is missing — exactly the fix the user bug required.
server.py:131-144 delete_file_from_doc is silent on failure (good) and covers both GridFS + disk, ensuring no orphans are left behind.
server.py:2027-2076 submission write path: old doc is deleted_from_doc BEFORE the new GridFS upload, preventing orphaned GridFS files on resubmission.

Minor: there are 4 pre-existing submissions in the DB with file_path only and no gridfs_id — those are legacy records that will return 410 (expected per handoff note). If the user wants a one-time migration of existing disk files into GridFS, that is out of scope of this fix but worth documenting.
Minor: server.py:41-42 UPLOAD_DIR is still created on startup even though nothing writes there anymore; can be removed in a follow-up cleanup but harmless.
test_credentials: Super admin slewis@theboostpad.org is already seeded in users collection. Tests create short-lived session tokens and a disposable student directly in Mongo (user_sessions + users) and clean up after themselves.
seed_data_creation: Per-run: one TEST cohort, one TEST_gridfs student user, one TEST library homework material (week 1, released), a test submission for each subtest. All seed data cleaned up at end of module via fixture teardown. Verified fs.files count returns to 0 after run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: GridFS migration verified. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_gridfs_storage.py is a reusable regression suite and takes ~14s. It calls the real AI review endpoint (GPT-5.2 via Emergent LLM key) — budget ~3-10s for that one test. Existing 4 submissions in DB with legacy file_path will always return 410 on download/review — that is expected behavior; do not flag as a bug.

rca_of_the_issue.original_bug: Instructor review showed 'Submission file not found on server. Please ask the student to resubmit.' because uploads were on ephemeral /app/backend/uploads/ and lost on Kubernetes redeploy.
rca_of_the_issue.fix_verified: save_bytes_to_gridfs/read_bytes_from_doc/delete_file_from_doc route all new writes through MongoDB GridFS (AsyncIOMotorGridFSBucket). All 4 write sites (library upload, library update, material upload, student submission, submit-on-behalf) store gridfs_id; all 3 read sites (material download, submission download, AI review + Coach Max context) read via read_bytes_from_doc which prefers gridfs_id and only falls back to file_path for legacy records.
rca_of_the_issue.persistence_check: Verified fs.files entry length matches uploaded bytes and download streams them back byte-for-byte. Deletion removes the GridFS entry (verified fs.files count returns to 0).
rca_of_the_issue.legacy_behavior: Legacy file_path-only records correctly surface HTTP 410 with clean instructor-facing message — no more scary 404 for current uploads.
